functions.name: decide_smallest_unit
functions.input: a row's stored text, a law snapshot, and optional context tie-breaks
functions.output: recopy with the smallest complete clause and its label, or a refusal reason
functions.if_none: no context given means several places stay refused as ambiguous_unit

functions.name: duplicate_problems
functions.input: plan rows, their section headers, and existing current rows
functions.output: list of clashes: same final key, or same document and same final text
functions.if_none: empty list when there are no clashes

functions.name: reprove
functions.input: the repaired plan rows and the visible-only page texts
functions.output: page_check on_page written for rows proven on their visible page
functions.if_none: rows not on the visible page are skipped and listed, never marked

functions.name: tiebreaks
functions.input: the row's ref_number (neighbour labels are accepted but no longer used)
functions.output: ordered list of own_label_unit then own_label hints
functions.if_none: empty list when the row's own label does not parse as a clause

break_it.scenario: the same standard is printed word for word in several codes and nothing in the row says which
break_it.what_happens: refused ambiguous_unit; the row stays shown with the citation-not-yet-checked mark
break_it.how: context must leave exactly one candidate; neighbour labels must agree

break_it.scenario: two plan rows would end holding the same law text
break_it.what_happens: the apply refuses before any write and names both ids
break_it.how: duplicate_problems checks final key and same document + same text

break_it.scenario: a council really printed a line twice (a table cell)
break_it.what_happens: kept: a pair is collapsed only when the doubled form is NOT on the visible page

break_it.scenario: a re-copy changes text under a structured numeric rule
break_it.what_happens: the write rolls back if DQ-108 rises
break_it.how: probe_108 before and after in the same transaction (both appliers)
break_it.repro: DQ-108 measured 0 after every write on 2026-10-17

mutation_analysis: Not executed. By reading: removing the 'neighbours must agree' condition fails test_neighbour_labels_break_a_tie_only_when_both_agree; dropping the white-colour filter fails test_white_span_is_dropped_dark_kept; removing the same-text rule fails test_same_text_different_labels_refused.
residual_risk: 81 SEPP rows remain ambiguous: the same standard sits in up to 6 codes and the row does not say which; the fix is to tie each such rule to its code(s), not to pick one. 28 Campbelltown rows were refused (collapsed text not one run of the visible page). About 30 council rows stay unresolved (words on several pages). Some Campbelltown rows with no repeated line were page-proven on text that includes the invisible copy. Cross-review 2026-10-17 (code-only, by hand): apply_visible_text_repair now re-derives each fix from the stored text and checks the PDF is the registry's file in force (the 94 written rows pass the stricter check against their pre-write backup); neighbour labels are limited to state-law rows (the one neighbour-settled row's document has 0 council rows); the LEP chain now reaches the complete-clause step after a ref-fix unit_too_big (re-run: 0 new rows). rules_lost: all 94 were 0 and the DQ-108 rollback guard covers it. Second cross-review pass: the neighbour-label tie-break is withdrawn (row id order is not document order) and its one row, 45999, reverted to its backup as version 3; the duplicate guard now also refuses same document + same text against SERVED rows outside the plan (9 such twins withheld, all already proven under loose labels); the Campbelltown re-proof fails if any row is skipped and runs automatically after a write. 17 groups of served rows with identical text in one document remain fleet-wide (Ashfield 10, state 3), not yet judged.
